tagline: Istanbul's ancient port and trading heart — the Spice Bazaar, Galata Bridge, ferry terminals, and the irresistible smell of simit and grilled mackerel.

items.name: Balık Ekmek (Galata Bridge)
items.description: Grilled mackerel sandwiches sold from boats moored under Galata Bridge. A true Istanbul street food ritual.
items.tip: Get your sandwich and eat it standing at the water's edge watching the ferries. This is the quintessential Istanbul snack.

items.name: Mısır Çarşısı (Spice Bazaar) — surrounding streets
items.description: The shops and stalls outside the Spice Bazaar sell nuts, dried fruits, cheeses, and pickles at far better prices than inside. The real market experience.
items.tip: The basement of the Spice Bazaar has excellent Turkish delight and spices at honest prices. The street stalls outside are where locals actually shop.

items.name: Hamdi Restaurant
items.description: A multi-storey restaurant above Eminönü with spectacular Golden Horn views. Reliable kebabs and mezes in an unbeatable location.
items.tip: Ask specifically for a window table with a view when booking. The food is good, the view is the reason to come.

items.name: Mısır Çarşısı (Egyptian Spice Bazaar)
items.description: One of Istanbul's oldest covered markets, built in 1660. Spices, Turkish delight, dried herbs, and teas in a stunning Ottoman interior.
items.tip: Browse rather than buy inside — prices are high for tourists. The streets outside the market are where the real deals are.

items.name: Galata Bridge Walk
items.description: Walk across Galata Bridge at any time of day — fishermen line the top railings, restaurants line the lower level, and ferries and ships pass below.

items.name: Ferry Departures (Eminönü İskelesi)
items.description: The main ferry hub of Istanbul — boats depart to Üsküdar, Kadıköy, Bosphorus villages, and the Princes' Islands. The ferry terminal itself is worth watching.
items.tip: The Bosphorus cruise boat (full Bosphorus ferry to Anadolu Kavağı) departs twice daily from pier 3. One of Istanbul's best experiences.

tips: Eminönü is best reached by tram (T1 line, Eminönü stop) or on foot from Karaköy across Galata Bridge.
The area is extremely busy during daytime — it's the main transit junction of the old city. Early morning is dramatic and uncrowded.
Everything in the Spice Bazaar costs more than elsewhere — negotiate or shop outside.
The side streets between Eminönü and Fatih are full of specialist traders selling spices, textiles, and hardware. Worth exploring.
